summary.title: My role as a founder CTO: Year Five
summary.one_liner: A founder CTO's year-five retrospective on RevenueCat covering team growth metrics, lessons from a support reorganization, parental leave, and the 2023 shipping plan.
takeaways: Team growth can be planned but may need scaling back in hard macro conditions; RevenueCat ended 2022 with 25 engineers versus a 34 target.
Moving support under engineering, with a self-serve/sold split and Zendesk as a single ticket system, improved morale and response times.
Replacing weekly one-on-ones with open office hours recovered calendar time, but regular one-on-ones with key people are still needed.
A VP of Engineering and documented processes let a founder CTO take leave and return to a company that kept operating.
Founders remain responsible for institutional knowledge, company values, and staying close to customers even after building the organization.
summary.summary: Miguel Carranza, a founder CTO of RevenueCat, reviews his fifth year in the role. He reports on the 2022 plan versus actual results using a metrics table (engineering team, company size, countries, time zones), then lists highlights and lowlights. The post covers changes made before and after his nine-week paternity leave, including office hours, a VP of Engineering, and reorganizing support under engineering. It ends with the 2023 focus on shipping and lessons learned about founder responsibilities. The page is a personal retrospective rather than a how-to guide.
